ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ ($a\ne 0$) has its axis of symmetry as the line $x=-1$, intersects with the $x$-axis at points $A$ and $B$, and intersects with the $y$-axis at point $C$. It is given that $OA=OC$, and the coordinates of point $A$ are $(-3,0)$. If point $P$ lies on the parabola, and the area of $\triangle POC$ is 4 times the area of $\triangle BOC$, what are the coordinates of point $P$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $x=0$, $y=-3$,\\
$\therefore$ point $C(0, -3)$, i.e., $OC=3$,\\
$\because$ A and B are symmetric about the axis of symmetry,\\
$\therefore$ B$(1,0)$, i.e., $OB=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle BOC}=\frac{1}{2}OB\times OC=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
Let $P(x,{x}^{2}+2x-3)$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle POC}=\frac{1}{2}\times3\times|x|$,\\
$\because$ $S_{\triangle POC}=4S_{\triangle BOC}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{3}{2}|x|=4\times \frac{3}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $x=\pm 4$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point $P$ are $\boxed{P(4,21)}$, $\boxed{P(-4,5)}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an upward-opening parabola, and the dashed line marks its axis of symmetry x=-1; the parabola intersects the x-axis at the left point A and the right point B, and intersects the y-axis at point C. In the figure, C is below the origin O, so C is on the negative half-axis of the y-axis. Reasoning: Given A=(-3,0), so OA=3. Also because OA=OC, OC=3. Combining with the fact that C is below O in the image, C=(0,-3) can be obtained. The axis of symmetry of the parabola is x=-1, and the x-coordinate of A is -3, so the other x-axis intersection point B is symmetric with A about x=-1; therefore the x-coordinate of B is 2(-1)-(-3)=1, so B=(1,0), OB=1. From the two zeros A(-3,0) and B(1,0), let the parabola be y=k(x+3)(x-1). Substitute C=(0,-3), to get -3=k·3·(-1)=-3k, therefore k=1. Thus the equation of the parabola is y=(x+3)(x-1)=x^2+2x-3. In triangle BOC, OB=1, OC=3, and OB is perpendicular to OC, so S_{△BOC}=1/2·1·3=3/2. Let P=(x,x^2+2x-3). Because OC is a vertical line segment on the y-axis, with length 3, the distance from point P to the y-axis is |x|, so S_{△POC}=1/2·3·|x|=3|x|/2. From the problem statement, S_{△POC}=4S_{△BOC}, that is, 3|x|/2=4·3/2=6, solving gives |x|=4, so x=4 or x=-4. Substitute into the parabola: when x=4, y=16+8-3=21; when x=-4, y=16-8-3=5.
